text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Jordan complained formally to Israel that opening of Jerusalem tunnel violated their peace agreement.
- Infrastructure Ministry checking on ownership of land near Jewish settlement of Ariel so that town can be expanded.
- Israeli army demanding control of hills around Hebron.
- Nestle looking into possibility of manufacturing chocolate in Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Jordan's King Hussein says peace with Israel in danger.
- Israeli air force helicopter to fly Palestinian President Arafat to meeting with Israeli president.
- Urgent economic talks today between Prime Minister Netanyahu and Israeli industrial leaders on cost of living increase, price freeze and devaluation.
- Fears of impending terror attack in Israel.
MAARIV
- Israeli President Weizman to meet Palestinian President Arafat today in Caesarea.
- Jewish lobby warns that Israeli-U.S. relations in danger.
- National Infrastructure Minister Sharon wants new Jerusalem-Tel Aviv railroad to pass through West bank; spokesman says no decision yet.
GLOBES
- Contacts under way for merger between Zim and large international company.
- Treasury to present original proposal on 1997 budget cut.
- Housing Ministry easing terms for contractors building private housing on its land in bid to increase housing starts.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Netanyahu, Labour leader Peres clash as new parliament session opens.
- Israel-PLO talks at Erez in high gear.
- Prime minister's adviser on terrorism warns of attacks.
- Israeli army not ready to resume joint patrols in West Bank.
